2607.02416.title: The Future of NLP may not be at NLP Conferences: Scholarly Migration Patterns in Natural Language Processing
2607.02416.paper_summary: Natural Language Processing (NLP) has traditionally been published in its core disciplinary venues like ACL. However, advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to a blurring of the disciplinary lines between NLP and general Machine Learning (ML), with authors regularly publishing in venues from both fields. Here, we ask whether the disciplinary center of gravity is shifting. Using NLP research published from 2010 to 2026 and studies of both established and new authors, we find that a migration is taking place. First, comparing the pre- and post-LLM eras, established authors lost 19.2pp of share at flagship *ACL main-conference tracks while gaining 14.8pp in the newer Findings tracks, and general ML venues rose 8.6pp, even when adjusting for parallel growth in the fields. Second, among newer authors who debut with at least three first-author NLP-topic papers, the share whose work appears mostly at *ACL venues fell from 84% (2019) to 74% (2024), while the share appearing mostly at general ML venues rose from 5% to 21%. Using causal inference techniques, we estimate that these general ML venues confer a significant citation premium, which influences venue selection. Together, these results point to a significant shift in where NLP research is published.
2607.02416.paper_summary_zh: 自然語言處理（NLP）傳統上在其核心學科的發表場所如ACL中出版。然而，大型語言模型（LLMs）的進步導致NLP與一般機器學習（ML）之間的學科界限變得模糊，作者們經常在這兩個領域的發表場所中發表作品。在這裡，我們詢問學科的重心是否正在轉變。使用2010年至2026年間發表的NLP研究，以及對既有作者和新作者的研究，我們發現正在發生一種遷移。首先，對比LLM前後的時期，既有作者在旗艦*ACL主會議的份額下降了19.2個百分點，而在較新的發現會議中增長了14.8個百分點，並且一般ML的發表場所上升了8.6個百分點，即使在調整了這些領域的平行增長之後。其次，在至少有三篇第一作者NLP主題論文的較新作者中，主要在*ACL發表的作品的份額從84%（2019年）下降到74%（2024年），而主要在一般ML發表的作品的份額從5%上升到21%。使用因果推斷技術，我們估計這些一般ML發表場所提供了顯著的引用溢價，這影響了發表場所的選擇。綜合這些結果，指向NLP研究發表地點的顯著轉變。
